reference_limitations: This is a source-only model proposal for reference-item design, not human-audited gold, an experimental evaluation, or a certification of applicable Indian law.
All proposed D-items have equal weight and binary satisfaction. The evidence witnesses, mandatory constraints and importance reasons do not create additional subpoints.

Each independently assessable substantive relation is a separate item. Necessary actor, property, document, default, procedural stage, polarity and legal condition bindings remain attached to the relation they qualify.

A report can satisfy an attributed-history item by accurately stating what a party pleaded or an earlier court held, even where that proposition's present legal effect remains unresolved. The report need not endorse the historical position.

Items D41, D42 and D44 assess materially relevant legal frameworks only at the level supported by the allowed texts. They do not require an unsupported conclusion that their statutory versions conclusively govern the historical tenancy.
Items D43 and D46 assess recognition of expressly identified open questions and the supported reasons for uncertainty. They do not require the hidden appellate result or hidden reasoning.
A historical report of waiver is assessed as historical reporting. Optional section 112 analysis cannot automatically replace the reported event or create a self-triggering additional point.

Exact incidental amounts, payment months, suit numbers, individual execution dates, tree-removal details and unrelated LAW provisions are retained as context where useful, but are not given independent equal-weight importance.

No essential obligation is conditional on whether a report happens to mention a particular optional statute. Affirmative unsupported legal assertions may be audited separately for correctness; their presence or absence does not change the fixed coverage denominator.

A shorter alternative reference that combines independent party allegations, court holdings or historical events would violate the supplied binary-item manual. A longer alternative that promotes every contextual payment, date, amount or procedural modification to an equal point would distort substantive importance.

Proposed items are not report scores. Their IDs and old-item mappings support later source review and uniform annotation without incorporating any system identity, method, output, score or preferred result.
The complete permitted CASE and LAW texts supplied in this request were used. No external browsing, case-memory completion, other-conversation material or hidden judgment inference was used.
